title: ‘मधेसतिर’ कथामा चार्वाक दर्शन {Charvak Philosophy in the story 'Madhestira'}
nepali: मधेसतिर कथामा चार्वाक दर्शन शीर्षकको यस आलेख पूर्वीय दर्शनअन्तर्गत चार्वाक दर्शनमा आधारितभई तयार गरिएको छ । विश्वेश्वरप्रसाद कोइरालाद्वारा लिखित मधेसतिर कथामा आएका विभिन्नपात्र सुखको खोजीमा मधेसतिर झरेको प्रसङ्ग कथामा प्रस्तुत छ । पूर्वीय दर्शनअन्तर्गत वैदिक रअवैदिक गरी दुई भेद रहेका छन् । पूर्वीय अवैदिक दर्शनमा बौद्ध, जैन र चार्वाक दर्शन पर्दछन् ।चार्वाक दर्शनसम्बन्धी विद्वानहरूका परिभाषा, मान्यता र विशेषतालाई यस अध्ययनमा समेटिएको छ ।चार्वाक दर्शनले वैदिक षड्दर्शनले राख्ने ईश्वर, आत्मा, पूर्वजन्म, पुनर्जन्म जस्ता मान्यतालाई अस्वीकार गर्दछ । भौतिकवादी दर्शनका रूपमा चिनिने यो दर्शनले राख्ने विभिन्न मान्यताहरूको निरूपण गर्दै मधेसतिर कथाका घटनाक्रम र त्यहाँ उपस्थित भएका विधवा, बूढो, भोटे, गोरे र धनेजस्ता पात्रका कार्यव्यापारहरूलाई चार्वाक मतका दृष्टिकोणबाट विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । {This article titled Charvak Darshan in Madhestir Katha has been prepared based on Charvak Darshan under Eastern philosophy. Written by Vishweshwar Prasad Koirala, the story of various characters who came to Madhes in search of happiness is presented in the story. There are two distinctions in Eastern philosophy, Vedic and Non-Vedic. Eastern non-Vedic philosophy includes Buddhist, Jain and Charvaka philosophy. The definitions, beliefs and characteristics of scholars related to Charvaka philosophy are included in this study. Charvaka philosophy rejects the beliefs of God, soul, pre-birth, reincarnation held by Vedic philosophy. Depicting the various beliefs held by this philosophy known as materialist philosophy, the events of the Madhestir story and the actions of the characters present there such as widows, old men, bhotes, whites and riches have been analyzed from the point of view of Charvak Mat.}
american_english: This article, titled "Charvaka Philosophy in the Story 'Madhestira'," has been prepared based on Charvaka philosophy within Eastern philosophy. In the story "Madhestira" written by Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala, the context of various characters descending toward the Madhesh in search of happiness is presented in the story. Under Eastern philosophy, there are two divisions, namely Vedic and non-Vedic. Eastern non-Vedic philosophy includes Buddhist, Jain, and Charvaka philosophies. Scholars' definitions, beliefs, and characteristics concerning Charvaka philosophy are incorporated in this study. Charvaka philosophy rejects beliefs such as God, soul, previous birth, and rebirth maintained by the six Vedic systems. Examining the various beliefs held by this philosophy known as a materialist philosophy, the sequence of events of the story "Madhestira" and the actions of characters appearing there—such as the Widow, the Old Man, Bhote, Gore, and Dhane—have been analyzed from the perspective of Charvaka thought.
